title: Sources on Tom Brown
summary: Allen cites Mrs. Brown's tape and other sources at Tulane and says Brown was among the earliest known.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, thank you, Johnny, very much. That's very flattering. But what I've done is collect these things, along with a lot of other people, and it's been a cooperative thing. And we were fortunate enough to have the help of Mrs. Tom Brown, who let us copy a tape interview with Tom Brown. And she gave us a lot of information. And, of course, we have old magazines, various jazz histories and books that have information on Tom Brown. And Eddie Chance can help you.
Would you say that Tom Brown was one of the first, or you'd say, um...

He certainly was one of the first ones that we know about today. Of course, see, people... Jazz was considered low-down music, and you weren't going to find anything written about it in the newspapers or in books. Fortunately, there were a few musicologists who were interested in the early days. And then...
